name: Notre-Dame de Paris and the Île de la Cité
note: Notre-Dame de Paris (1163-1345, restored and reopened December 2024 with Viollet-le-Duc's spire rebuilt, 96 m) on the Île de la Cité, seen at dusk from the Seine's left bank by the Pont de la Tournelle: the chevet and its flying buttresses over the Square Jean-XXIII, the twin west towers (69 m), the river with its quais, the Pont de l'Archevêché, the Pont au Double and the Pont Saint-Louis, the Île Saint-Louis's hôtels particuliers to the east, the Hôtel-Dieu and the Conciergerie and Sainte-Chapelle beyond, the Latin Quarter's Haussmann blocks on the left bank and the Hôtel de Ville on the right. Scale 1.4 blocks per metre; 1680 blocks a side (half 600 m), centred between the cathedral and the bridge. IGN LiDAR HD, BD ORTHO and BD TOPO (every building's height). Turned -26 degrees so the cathedral's axis (its nave's outline reads 25-28 degrees south of east) runs along x: its long walls are straight, not staircases.
